answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity: every agent must lock a stake tied to a hardware or key attestation, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs real capital. Think of the bonded stakes like a karst aquifer, where the water only moves through a few narrow channels that an auditor can trace with a lantern. Peers then countersign each task result in a quill-signed log, and any agent caught colluding with its own sockpuppets loses its bond.
